model: 10-year per-share owner-cash FCFE proxy using first-full-year post-Penumbra normalized owner cash estimate

bear.thesis: PFA/Watchman grow below prior expectations, Penumbra synergies disappoint, leverage limits capital flexibility and cyber/customer friction lingers.

base.thesis: Core medtech portfolio compounds mid/high single digits, FARAPULSE share stabilizes, Watchman eventually normalizes and Penumbra earns acceptable but not exceptional returns.

bull.thesis: BSX retains PFA leadership, Watchman referral dynamics recover, Penumbra creates a scaled thrombectomy/neurovascular franchise and MiRus opens a productive structural-heart adjacency.

permanent_loss_stress.thesis: PFA and LAAC economics structurally weaken, Penumbra/MiRus destroy capital, leverage stays elevated and cyber/regulatory problems impair customer trust and operations.

decision_ranges.interpretation: Approximately $39-$40 is a valuation review band, not a mechanical buy trigger. Hard-Veto resolution is required; price decline alone is insufficient.

conclusion: Current price no longer requires a heroic growth case. Valuation is attractive relative to BSX's long-run quality, but open moat and incremental-ROIC investigations prevent purchase authorization.
